newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis set new targets for Greece in the next 18 months when he pledged on Saturday that the country would meet Maastricht criteria by the end of 1998. Additional corrective measures and the new mix of economic policies, according to sources, will have to be shaped within the next few months to be included in the new budget.

--"A storm in a teacup" is how National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou characterised the response last week to the release of the recommendations of economics professor Yiannis Spraos's report on convergence for the Greek economy.

--The slowing rate of deceleration of inflation is forcing banks in new directions vis-a-vis their interest rates policies. The National Bank's recent decision to drop rates for good clients is one likely to be imitated by other banks. KATHIMERINI (Sunday)

--The Spraos report has caused friction within the government with Papandoniou reportedly dissatisfied with the timing of the release of the report and the issues its raises shortly before the drafting of a new budget.

--The submission in Parliament of a draft bill on public works, the ratification of tenders worth 51 billion drachmas, and Hochtief - the German consortium building the Spata airport - commissioning work by Greek firms all bode well for construction companies.

--Profits for commercial banks will see a significant increase in 1997; National announced profits were up 89 percent in the first five months of the year while Commercial expects a four-fold increase in the first half-year, equal to 1996's entire profits. However, money remains expensives with the fate of interest rates tied to inflation, which looks set to stall at present levels for the second half-year.

--The Athens Stock Exchange's good showing this year has provided a breather for brokerage firms after the trials of 1996: howevcer, smaller firms continue to face the prospect of emrgers as the only viable choice.
--The failure to index-link the tax scale for 1996 means a greater burden for wage-earners, who will pay up to 31.7 percent more tax this year.
--Interest in the Greek stock exchange is increasing with international investors confident that the market has good medium-term prospects. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
